2473: Satoshi (known as Ash Ketchum in most international territories) is the main character of the Pocket Monsters anime.
2909: Kasumi is a Gym Leader of Hanada City's Gym, known officially as the Hanada Gym. She gives the Cascade Badge to Trainers who defeat her in battle. She specializes in Water-type Pokémon. Kasumi is a friend and former traveling partner of the anime's main character, Satoshi.
3854: Takeshi appeared primarily as an opponent to Satoshi in his debut episode; unlike later Gym Leaders, he requested to join Satoshi on his journey, aiming to be the world's greatest Pokémon Breeder.
3891: Pikachu is the signature Pokémon of the Pocket Monsters anime, and the first Pokémon that Satoshi obtained on his journey as a Pokémon Trainer, given to him by Professor Okido.
3935: Musashi is a member of the Rocket Gang, more specifically part of a trio with Kojirou and Nyarth, that follows Satoshi and his friends around in the Pocket Monsters anime, usually trying to steal Satoshi's Pikachu.
3936: Kojirou is a member of the Rocket Gang, more specifically part of a trio with Musashi and Nyarth, that follows Satoshi and his friends around in the Pocket Monsters anime, usually trying to steal Satoshi's Pikachu.
3937: Nyarth is a member of Rocket-dan (Team Rocket), more specifically part of a trio with Musashi and Kojirou, that follows Satoshi and his friends around in the Pokémon anime, usually trying to steal Satoshi's Pikachu.
5113: Mewtwo is a Pokémon created by science. Mewtwo was created after years of horrific gene splicing and DNA engineering experiments based on Mew. It is said to have the most savage heart among all Pokémon, lack compassion, and strike fear into its enemy with cold, glowing eyes.
7040: Shiba is a member of the Kanto Elite Four. He raises Fighting-type Pokémon, living with them and training with them. He joined the Elite Four out of a desire to challenge the best Trainers. Although he trains Fighting Pokémon, he also commonly uses Iwark and its evolved form.
7041: Kanna is an Ice-type Trainer and the first member of the Indigo Elite Four. Kanna's skills are highly regarded and she makes frequent appearances in the media, though she is dismissive of her fame and the praise of others.
7042: Wataru is a Dragon-type Trainer, a member of the Indigo Elite Four, the Pokémon Champion of the Indigo Plateau and also a member of the Pokémon G-Men detective organization. He specializes in Dragon-type Pokémon.
7558: Nurse Joy is a recurring character in every Pokemon series released. There are multiple Nurse Joys in every town, city and region. They all look the same, have the same voice and personalities.
8365: Mew, Psychic-type legendary Pokemon Mewtwo Strikes Back, Mew made a couple cameo appearances at the start of the movie. A Mewtwo was cloned from Mew's DNA, extracted from Mew's eyelash.
8674: Very little is known about Kosaburo's early life. At one point in time, he was training to become a Rocket member at the same time as Musashi, Kojiro, and Yamato. Yamato and Kosaburo were assigned together and now work as a team, capturing Pokémon for Team Rocket.
9881: Sakaki is the Rocket Team Boss and a former Tokiwa City Gym Leader. He is a very ambitious man and is intolerant of failure. Sakaki is shown to have access to vast wealth and resources.
12128: Hayato is the Gym Leader of Violet City's Gym, known officially as the Violet Gym. He hands out the Zephyr Badge to Trainers who defeat him. He specializes in Flying-type Pokémon. Hayato has a self-righteous attitude when it comes to Pokémon training, which angered Satoshi.
14111: Katsura is the Gym Leader of Guren Island's (later the Twin Islands') Gym, known officially as the Guren Gym. He hands out the Volcano Badge to Trainers who defeat him. He is a highly intelligent man who specializes in Fire-type Pokémon.
17112: Natsume is the Gym Leader of Yamabuki City's Gym, known officially as the Yamabuki Gym. She hands out the Marsh Badge to Trainers who defeat her. She possesses psychic abilities and specializes in Psychic-type Pokémon.
17282: Matis is the Gym Leader of Kuchiba City's Gym, known officially as the Kuchiba Gym. He hands out the Thunder Badge to Trainers who defeat him. He specializes in Electric-type Pokémon. An intimidating person, Matis surrounds himself with other tough-looking Trainers.
17283: Erika is the Gym Leader of Celadon City's Gym, known officially as the Celadon Gym. She hands out the Rainbow Badge to trainers who defeat her. She is a serene young woman who specializes in Grass-type Pokémon.
17284: Kyou was the Leader of Sekichiku City's Gym. He is a student of ninjutsu who specializes in Poison-type Pokémon. He handed out the Soul Badge to Trainers who defeated him.
17783: Yukinari Ookido is a Pokémon Professor and a major supporting character of the Pocket Monsters anime who lives and works at his research lab in Masara Town. He appears semi-regularly to give Satoshi advice to help him achieve his goal of becoming the greatest Pokémon Master.
18906: Bugsy (Tsukushi in original Japanese language versions) is in charge of the Hive Badge, and resides in Azalea Town. He is an expert on Bug-type Pokémon. His name derives from the word bug.
18907: Whitney (Akane in original Japanese language versions) is in charge of the Plain Badge, and resides in Goldenrod City. (The Plain Badge's name is a pun in English; Whitney lives on a rural Midwestern-esque farm, and is also a trainer of Normal-type Pokémon.
18908: Jasmine (Mikan in original Japanese language versions) is in charge of the Mineral Badge (Steel Badge in Japanese), and resides in Olivine City. She is an expert on Steel types, but also has an Ampharos which lights the Olivine Lighthouse.
18909: Claire (Ibuki in original Japanese language versions) is in charge of the Rising Badge, and resides in Blackthorn City. She is an expert on Dragon types. Lance, the head of the Kanto Elite Four, is her cousin, and she once trained with him for the Elite Four.
19852: While Brock was at Professor Ivy's lab, Ash and Misty land on Tangelo Island and meet this young man, Tracey. He is a Pokemon Watcher and is also a very big fan of Professor Oak.
20514: In the original Japanese version, Casey speaks with a Kansai dialect, which would suggest that she is from the Pokémon world's equivalent of Osaka, Goldenrod City.
26545: Officer Jenny is not a single entity. Rather, there are many Jennys working as police officers across the various regions of the Pokémon world. Generally, Officer Jennies are brave and determined, but mostly ineffective in their police duties.
29184: She is Ash's mother. Delia is very caring of her son, always reminding him to do his best. She is very talented, having won a beauty pageant and cooked a dish so popular that elite chefs at the Indigo Plateau have asked for its recipe.
30978: A school girl who attends a school called the Pokémon Technical Institute which is located somewhere between Cerulean City and Vermilion City. She is a character of the day in The School of Hard Knocks. She also appears in the Electric Tale of Pikachu manga.
31689: Morty (Matsuba in the Japanese version of Pokemon) is the Gym Leader of Ecruteak City's Gym, known officially as the Ecruteak Gym. He hands out the Fog Badge to Trainers who defeat him. He is a young man who uses Ghost-type Pokemon.
34671: Ritchie first appeared in A Friend In Deed and quickly befriended his fellow Pokémon League competitor, Ash Ketchum. This led to problems in the next episode, Friend or Foe Alike, since the two were matched up to battle against each other.
34677: Her first appearance was in Ditto's Mysterious Mansion. Ash and his friends were traveling through Kanto when they sought shelter from the rain in an abandoned mansion. The house was actually called "The House of Imite" and it was owned by Duplica and her Ditto.
34707: Suzy is a famous Pokemon Breeder. In her first appearance, Brock asked to become her apprentice. Unfortunately she declined the offer. However, did ask Brock for him to help raise her Vulpix. On Suzy's return to a Breeder competition, Brock returned her Vulpix.
34708: Jessiebelle is James's fiance (arranged by their parents). They've known each other since they were children but James was not digging the marriage scene so he leaves. Jessiebelle prepares for the day where the two of them can be together.
34710: Professor Ivy is the Pokémon professor on Valencia Island (in the Orange Islands). She is a close friend of Professor Oak's. When Ash and the gang came to her lab, they picked up a mysterious pokeball.
35797: Corey was one of the only Trainers to make it to New Island. He made it by flying on the back of his Pidgeot. Along with Neesha, Fergus, and Ash and his friends, Corey witnessed the revelation that Mewtwo was trying to destroy the world.
35798: Neesha, along with Corey, Fergus, and Ash and his friends were the only Pokémon Trainers who were able to make it to New Island. She made it to New Island by riding on her Dewgong's back.
35800: Fergus was one of the only Pokémon Trainers who was able to make it through Mewtwo's storm and reach New Island, along with Ash, his friends, Neesha and Corey.
35802: While Ash and his friends were waiting to eat, he approached them and asked Ash for a battle.
36309: This character page is set to represent and list all narrators, which haven't been given a visual representation of themselves in their respective work.
53521: Togepy is a small, light yellow Pokémon with a round body that is still encased in its eggshell. Togepy does not shed its shell. The Egg has red and blue shapes on it. Togepy has stubby hands and round feet with two toes each.
136296: Koduck is a yellow Pokémon resembling a duck or bipedal platypus. On top of its head are three thick strands of black hair and it has a wide, flat cream-colored beak. Its eyes seem vacant and have tiny pupils. Its legs and tail are stubby, and it has cream-colored webbed feet.
142475: Kairyu is a draconic, bipedal Pokémon with light orange skin. It has large, grayish-green eyes and a round snout with small nostrils. A pair of long, thin antennae sprout from the top of its head with a small horn set between them.
144635: Sonans is a tall, cyan Pokémon with a soft body. Its eyes usually appear scrunched, and it has a jagged upper lip. Female Sonans have a red marking on their mouth that resembles lipstick, while males do not.
146407: The wife of Dr. Fuji and the mother of the late Ai. When Dr. Fuji dedicated his life to resurrecting Ai, she decided she could no longer be his wife and left him, leaving behind her wedding ring.
146408: Ai was the daughter of Dr. Fuji, who died while she was still a child.
149425: Leon is Hiroshi's main Pokémon, a Pikachu. It is distinguished from other Pikachu by a scruff of fur on the top of its head.
149426: Zippo is Hiroshi's Lizardo. It first appeared as a Hitokage, and evolved by the time Satoshi and Hiroshi met in the Whirlpool Islands.
149752: Michael is at least twenty years old, having been first found by surfing enthusiast Vincent shortly after he failed to conquer a large wave, "Humungadunga". Vincent was trying to emulate a feat achieved by his surfing hero Jan two decades ago.
149753: The pink Butterfree is the first alternately colored Pokémon in the anime. It was created before alternately colored Pokémon appeared in the games, possibly to differentiate it from the other Butterfree in the episode.
149754: Purin is a pink Pokémon with a spherical body. It has pointed ears with black insides and large, blue eyes. It has small, stubby arms and slightly longer feet. On top of its head is a curled tuft of fur.
149757: Beroringa is a bipedal Pokémon with a round body and a thick, powerful tail. It has soft, pink skin with curved yellow lines on its belly and a yellow ring marking on each knee. It has a thumb-like claw on each hand and a single large nail on each foot.
152206: Barri-chan is a Barrierd who is currently living with Satoshi's mother Hanako.
160842: After being forced to evolve as a part of an experiment by Rocket-dan, this Gyarados went on rampage until Wataru managed to catch it. It was later used to help stop the battle between Kyogre and Groudon.
177028: Sunnygo is a small, pink, roundish Pokémon with branch-like growths on its back, which are similar to coral. There is a smaller, blunt horn on its forehead, and it has black, oval eyes. It has a white underside, which speckles towards the sides.
177034: Heracros is a bipedal, beetle-like Pokémon covered in a blue exoskeleton. There is a long, pronged horn on its forehead. The horn ends in a cross on the male and a heart-shape in the female. On either side of the horn is a short antenna with a spherical tip.
177035: Hinoarashi is a small, bipedal Pokémon with bluish fur on top of its body and cream-colored fur on its underside. Its eyes are usually seen closed, and it has a long, thin snout. Its arms are short, but its legs are slightly more developed and have a single nail on each foot.
177037: Kabigon is a huge, bipedal, dark blue-green Pokémon with a cream-colored face, belly, and feet. Its body is composed of mostly its belly, as its limbs are comparatively small. Its head is large with small, pointed ears and two pointed teeth protruding from its lower jaw.
177038: Fushigidane is a small, quadruped Pokémon that has blue-green skin with darker patches. It has red eyes with white pupils, pointed, ear-like structures on top of its head, and a short, blunt snout with a wide mouth.
177039: Betbeton is a large, sticky, amorphous Pokémon made of living purple sludge. It has two small eyes with beady black pupils. It also has an enormous mouth with a gray tongue and strands of ooze connecting its top and bottom jaws.
177041: Waninoko is a bipedal, crocodilian Pokémon with well-developed jaws. It has red eyes with ridges above them, black markings around its eyes, and several sharp teeth.
180037: Lizardon is a draconic, bipedal Pokémon. It is primarily orange with a cream underside from the chest to the tip of its tail. It has a long neck, small blue eyes, slightly raised nostrils, and two horn-like structures protruding from the back of its rectangular head.
180469: Iwark is a Pokémon composed of a giant chain of gray boulders that become smaller towards the tail. Its length makes it the tallest Rock-type Pokémon. It has black eyes and a rounded snout. On top of its head is a rocky spine.
181415: Zenigame is a small Pokémon that resembles a light blue turtle. It has large, purplish or reddish eyes and a slightly hooked upper lip. Each of its hands and feet have three pointed digits. The end of its long tail curls inward.
181416: Kingler is a crustacean Pokémon resembling a crab. Its strong shell covers the outside of its body, featuring a red upper half and a light tan lower half. Its upper half is topped with six tall, thin spikes that resemble a crown.
181417: Butterfree resembles a vaguely anthropomorphic butterfly with a purple body. Unlike true insects, it only has two body segments and four light blue legs. The upper pair of legs resemble small, three-fingered hands, while the lower pair resembles long, digit-less feet.
181419: Pigeon is a raptor-like avian Pokémon. It is covered with brown feathers, has a cream-colored face, underside, and flight feathers. It has a crest of pinkish-red feathers on its head and black, angular markings behind its eyes.
181700: Gar-chae is a Gardie that was owned by a younger Kojirou and his first Pokémon. Eventually, Kojirou ran away from home, leaving behind his beloved Gardie.
181802: Crobat is a purple, bat-like Pokémon with a small, round body. It has long, pointed ears, yellow eyes with red pupils, and a small mouth that usually has its teeth bared.
183410: Nyorozo is a blue, bipedal Pokémon with a spherical body. It has bulbous eyes that protrude from the top of its head. A black and white swirl covers its belly, which is actually its organs showing through its thin skin.
183412: Rokon is a small, quadruped, fox-like Pokémon. It has a red-brown pelt with a cream-colored underbelly. It has brown eyes, large, pointed ears with dark brown insides, and a triangular dark brown nose.
183414: Matadogas is a purple Pokémon consisting of two spherical heads connected by a thin tube with another sphere in the center. The heads have differing sizes and features.
183415: Arbok is a serpentine Pokémon that resembles a cobra. It has narrow eyes and several sharp teeth. Just below its head is a large hood with a face-like pattern. This pattern has over 20 possible variations.
190816: Chicorita is a small, pale green Pokémon with dark green buds around its neck. Its head is large in proportion to the rest of its body, and it has big red eyes. It has four short legs with a single nailed toe on each and a stubby tail.
224575: Laplace is a large sea Pokémon that resembles a plesiosaur. It has a blue hide with darker blue spots and a cream-colored underside. It has large brown eyes, a short horn on its forehead, and tightly curled ears. It has a long neck and four flippers.
